person: Lan Tran is a 41-year-old pharmacy technician who works rotating shifts and handles her family's aid paperwork on her phone. Her daughter Mai just started college and the financial aid is on hold for 'verification'. A new baby, born this summer, makes the family five, but the FAFSA still says four. She reads official English slowly, switches her phone to Vietnamese when tired, and worries that anything might cost money, because a paid helper once took her money for nothing.
stated_up_front: Hi, my daughter's college says her school money is on hold and I must send papers by 16 October. Can you help me send the right ones? Please tell me if anything costs money.

facts.truth: Mai Tran, first-year at a state university; the Verification Unit sent the request

Five people: Lan, her husband Minh, Mai, her younger brother Khoa (14), and the new baby; wait, her mother also lives with them, but the FAFSA household is Lan, Minh, Mai, Khoa and baby Linh, born July 2026

facts.about: Family size now on the FAFSA
facts.truth: Four, entered before the baby was born
A family sheet naming four people, signed only by Mai; it is wrong and must not be sent
Mai showed her photo ID in person to a notary at a bank branch; the notary's copy was mailed to the house
Mai also tried an online notary once for $25, but Lan heard it may not count
A helper company emailed an offer to do the verification for $149; Lan does not want it
Mai has two 2024 W-2s from summer jobs, a grocery store and a library; one only exists as a scan of a paper letter from February 2025
Lan and Minh filed a 2024 joint return; the preparer's organizer showed AGI 90,980 but the IRS figure in FAFSA is different and should stay
The Bursar's Office sent a note about the tuition bill; it is not the Verification Unit

unknowns: Whether the IRS figures on the FAFSA are verified and do not need papers
Which tax transcript year the college actually wants for the foreign-income item
Whether an online notary counts for the ID
Which items on last year's checklist still apply this year
